title: Settlers Besiege Three Palestinian Families in Qusra for Fourth Day, Cutting Water and Power
detail: A settler siege of three Palestinian families in Qusra, south of Nablus, entered its fourth day on August 13, 2026. Extremist settlers erected makeshift structures blocking entrances to the homes of Youssef Hassan (with his wife and two young daughters) and the Abu Rida/Abu Ridi families beginning Sunday, August 9–10, cutting off water and electricity in what residents called an attempt to seize their land. IDF and Border Police entered Qusra for a three-day operation to clear settler outposts and, on Wednesday, dismantled settler tents and deployed an additional infantry battalion, calling the settler activity 'illegal, reprehensible and unacceptable.' Despite this, hours after the IDF said troops would not occupy the families' houses, the Hassan family remained unable to return to their own home and stayed in a third, empty house in the compound. One besieged family reported only two to three days of food remaining.

media.caption: Palestinian families remain besieged by settlers in their homes in Qusra, West Bank — August 13, 2026

title: Israel Officially Reopens Ganim Settlement, 21 Years After 2005 Evacuation
detail: Israel held an official reopening ceremony for the West Bank settlement of Ganim, near Jenin, on August 13, 2026 — more than two decades after it was evacuated under Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's 2005 disengagement plan. About two dozen prefabricated homes have already been installed, with construction machinery clearing space for more on the hillside. Roughly 100 people attended, including Defense Minister Israel Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli settlement authority for the northern West Bank. Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government, three of the four settlements evacuated in 2005 — Ganim, Sa-Nur, and Homesh — have now been officially re-established. Palestinians in the valley below told reporters they fear the settlement's growth will worsen their lives or lead to displacement.

media.caption: Israeli officials and settlers attend the reopening ceremony of the Ganim settlement near Jenin, 21 years after its 2005 evacuation — August 13, 2026
